# intra-mart Accel Platform Development Project

## Overview

This project develops on the intra-mart Accel Platform, combining the following development models.

| Development Model | Use |
|------|------------|
| JSSP (script development model) | Source code for screens and various plugins |
| Java (JavaEE development model) | Source code for various plugins (excluding screens) |
| IM-LogicDesigner / IM-Workflow / IM-BPM | Low-code assets |

## Technology Stack

### JSSP (script development model)

| Item | Technology |
|------|------------|
| Server-side | Rhino JavaScript (ES5 compatible) |
| Template | IMART tags |
| Database | TenantDatabase / SharedDatabase API |
| File Operations | SystemStorage / PublicStorage / SessionScopeStorage API |
| Workflow | IM-Workflow / ApplyManager |
| Low-code | IM-LogicDesigner |

### Java (JavaEE development model)

See `.github/instructions/java-architecture.instructions.md` for details. For layer structure, dependency rules, naming conventions, etc., see the Java conventions listed in `.github/instructions/README.md`.

## Mandatory Rules (No Exceptions, TSSP)

When TSSP files (`.ts` / `.html` under `src/main/tssp/src`) are **newly generated or edited**, the following steps **must be executed**. Step 1 is done before implementation; steps 2–5 are done before reporting completion.
Skipping or deferring is prohibited regardless of context compression, session resumption, or the volume of work.

1. List the APIs to be used, Read the corresponding files under `d.ts/`, and note their signatures (do not write APIs from memory).
2. Run the `tssp:dev` script in package.json (`tssp build --dev`) and get a successful build with 0 type errors and 0 Rhino lint violations. Do not work around type errors with `any` / `as any` / `@ts-ignore` / `@ts-expect-error` / `@ts-nocheck` / your own `declare`.
3. Run the `tssp-page-verifier` skill via a sub-agent and fix all issues until the error count reaches 0.
4. Run the `tssp-code-review` skill if available.
5. Run the `jssp-security-check` skill if available.

> For the steps that run skills, a step may be skipped only if the skill itself does not exist. Skipping for reasons such as "it takes too long" or "there are too many files" is not permitted.

## Using TSSP Skills vs. JSSP Skills

There are four TSSP skills: `tssp-usage` / `tssp-page-generator` / `tssp-page-verifier` / `tssp-code-review`. For work where a TSSP skill exists, always use the TSSP skill.
Apply the other `jssp-*` skills and the conventions in `.github/instructions/` by reinterpreting them as TypeScript where appropriate. Follow `.github/instructions/tssp-typescript.instructions.md` for how to write the reinterpreted code. Do not disclose that this reinterpretation was done.

- Rewrite the JSSP (`.js`) code examples produced by a reinterpreted skill into `.ts` before using them.
- Run `jssp-security-check` against the build output under `src/main/jssp/src` and the `.html` files.

## Sub-Agent Split Policy (TSSP)

For large-scale TSSP implementations involving multiple files, delegate work to sub-agents as described below to prevent the main conversation context from growing too large.

### Execution Order (strict — dependencies require this order)

```
① DDL / SQL agent               ← Always first (foundation for screens, APIs, and batch jobs)
         ↓ after completion
② The following can run in parallel:
   ├─ Screen agent               (view/*.ts + view/*.html)
   ├─ API agent                  (api/*.ts)
   ├─ Batch agent                (job/*.ts)
   └─ Workflow agent             (workflow/ directory — only when using IM-Workflow)
         ↓ after completion
③ Routing / tenant setup agent
   (routing-jssp-config/*.xml, roles, authorization, menu, job settings)
         ↓ after completion
④ Verification agent            ← Mandatory — no exceptions
   (tssp-page-verifier → tssp-code-review → jssp-security-check)
```

### Responsible Skills per Sub-Agent

| Sub-Agent | Scope | Skill |
|-----------|-------|-------|
| DDL/SQL | DDL (3 dialects), SQL templates, sample DML | `tssp-page-generator` (step 6) |
| Screen | `view/*.ts` + `view/*.html` | `tssp-page-generator` (steps 1–5) |
| API | `api/*.ts` | `tssp-page-generator` (API variant) |
| Batch | `job/*.ts` | `jssp-im-job-generator` |
| Workflow | `workflow/` directory | `jssp-im-workflow-usage` |
| Routing / tenant setup | `routing-jssp-config/*.xml`, tenant materials | `jssp-tenant-setup-generator` |
| Verification | Validate and fix all deliverables | `tssp-page-verifier` / `tssp-code-review` / `jssp-security-check` |

### Notes

- Screen and API agents must reference the table names, column names, and SQL template paths generated by the DDL/SQL agent.
- When briefing each sub-agent, explicitly pass the dependent artifacts (DDL paths, SQL template paths, etc.).
- If the number of files per agent is large, it is acceptable to split further by functional area (e.g., master data vs. request processing).
- A sub-agent that writes `.ts` must run the `tssp:dev` script in package.json before reporting, and get 0 type errors and 0 Rhino lint violations for its assigned files.
- `src/main/jssp/src` is the output destination of `tssp build`, so do not edit it by hand. Place by hand only the files that `tssp build` does not output (2WaySQL `.sql` files go in `src/main/jssp/src/{feature-name}/sql/`; the extension imports `*_import.js` for tenant environment setup and `source-config.xml` go in their usual locations). Place `.ts` and `.html` files in `src/main/tssp/src`.

### API Type Definitions (d.ts, TSSP)

When implementing TSSP function containers (`.ts`), refer to the TypeScript type definition files under `d.ts/`.
These define the API specifications (arguments, return values, and types) for globally available classes, functions, and objects in SSJS.
The tsconfig used for type checking in `tssp build` includes `d.ts/**/*.d.ts`, so using an API that is not in the d.ts files (or in the tsconfig `lib`) makes `tssp build` fail. Types with an index signature, such as `Request`, pass type checking even for method names that are not declared, so verify method names in the d.ts files.

| Directory | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `d.ts/platform/` | Platform standard APIs (Database, Storage, HTTP, Mail, etc.) |
| `d.ts/tenant/` | Tenant management APIs (Account, Menu, Calendar, Password, etc.) |

**Notes:**
- Before implementing, list the APIs to be used, Read the corresponding d.ts files, and note the signatures (arguments, return values, and types).
- Do not work around type checking with `any` / `as any` / `@ts-ignore` / `@ts-expect-error` / `@ts-nocheck` / your own `declare`.
- d.ts files should only be used for function container (`.ts`) implementation, not for presentation page (`.html`) implementation.
